A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CLEAR and contain 73 pages, including Appendices A–I. Full text comparison and rendered-page checks support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulations, experiments on 17 regression datasets, and an Ames Housing case study, with detailed results in Appendices C–H.

after.justification: v4 retains the original simulations, 17-dataset experiments, and Ames Housing case study, including their appendix results.

M1.justification: CLEAR’s uncertainty estimators, two-parameter calibration, and parameter selection remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 merely rewrites the loss normalization from division by the sample count followed by division by two to division by twice the sample count.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same homoskedastic, heteroskedastic, and multivariate simulations, 17 real-world regression datasets, and Ames Housing scenarios varying features and training-data availability.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same PCS, ALEATORIC, ALEATORIC-R, Naive, fixed-parameter, UACQR-P/S, and DE/SQR comparators and conformalized variants. Appendix A.3.3 corrects EPISCORE to EPICSCORE for the same cited work; it does not introduce another comparator.

E3.justification: Splits, preprocessing, model configurations, calibration procedures, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Section 2.1 corrects the background description of CQR; CLEAR’s existing calibration rule in Algorithm 1 and Appendix B.5 is retained.

E4.justification: The fixed-parameter ablations, model variants (a)–(c), extrapolation and heteroskedasticity analyses, and Ames Housing feature/sample-size study retain the same questions and evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 100-simulation averaging, the reported 10-seed benchmark evaluations, mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, and median/minimum/maximum parameter summaries. No run-count or statistical-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains NCIW improvements of 28.57% over DE and 13.36% over SQR; the detailed benchmark and case-study results are also identical.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 replaces CQR’s requirement to cover exactly the specified number of calibration points with the smallest calibration value covering at least that number, correcting the definition for tied scores. Theorems and proof arguments otherwise remain unchanged; Appendix B.2’s r-to-q replacement is a notation correction.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about two-parameter calibration, residual-based aleatoric estimation, PCS integration, conditional coverage, and benchmark performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of adaptive uncertainty weighting and the limitations concerning base-estimator quality, small calibration sets, exchangeability, scalability, and additive combination are retained. No substantive explanation or qualification is added.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and runtime reporting, data-processing instructions, and project/code access information remain unchanged in the main text and appendices.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. Correcting EPISCORE to EPICSCORE in Appendix A.3.3 preserves the same Cabezas et al. (2025) reference, comparison, and interpretation.

P1.justification: v4 adds Ilia Azizi’s BegooAI affiliation and makes localized wording, spelling, and notation corrections, including Table 5 and Appendices A.3, B.2, and F. Section organization and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The added affiliation shifts first-page content and moves one introduction line onto page 2. Algorithm 1’s loss fraction is typeset differently. Figures and result-table structures are unchanged, with no substantial layout redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves mathematical precision by replacing Section 2.1’s exact-count CQR rule with a minimum calibration value satisfying an at-least threshold, avoiding ambiguity with ties. Terminology, notation, and grammar corrections further improve clarity. The method, empirical evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
